newsitem.title: USA: Transco seeks rate increase, backhaul pay.
newsitem.headline: Transco seeks rate increase, backhaul pay.

text.p: Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Corp said Friday it submitted to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission a general rate case filing principally designed to recover costs associated with increased capital expenditures.
The filing also includes proposals to roll-in the costs of Transco's Leidy Line and Southern expansion incremental projects and to make interruptible backhaul rates equal to the forward haul rates.
A spokeswoman noted the pipeline now performs interruptible backhaul at no cost to its customers.
The Williams Cos Inc subsidiary said the increased capital expenditures primarily relate to system reliability, integrity and Clean Air Act compliance.

When stated on a comparable basis, the general rate filing proposes an annual cost of service increase of about $67 million over the cost of service underlying the rates contained in the pending settlement of Transco's last general rate filing.
The rates are expected to become effective, subject to refund, on May 1, assuming a five-month suspension. They are designed using the straight fixed-variable rate design method.

Transo described the portions of the filing dealing with its incremental projects and backhaul rates as "pro-forma proposals," explaining they would become effective prospectively only after final FERC approval.
